questions.prompt: Which example of prompt chaining does Anthropic give that fits localised ads?

options.text: Sending refund requests and technical questions down two paths
options.explanation: That is Anthropic's example for routing, not for prompt chaining.

options.text: Several different prompts each reviewing the same code for weak points
options.explanation: That is a voting example from the parallelization workflow.

options.text: Generating marketing copy, then translating it to another language
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic lists this as a prompt chaining example. One call writes the copy and the next call translates it.

questions.prompt: What is the main goal of prompt chaining, according to Anthropic?

options.text: To run all the steps at the same moment so the whole job ends sooner
options.explanation: That describes parallelization. A chain runs the steps one after the other.

options.text: To trade some latency for higher accuracy, with each call an easier task
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says the goal is to trade latency for higher accuracy by making each LLM call an easier task.

options.text: To skip checks, because each step feeds the next and so nothing can go wrong
options.explanation: Anthropic says you can add programmatic checks, called gates, on any step of the chain.

questions.prompt: Why does OpenAI say to orchestrate through code when the steps are known?

options.text: Code lets the model choose a new set of steps for each new item
options.explanation: That is orchestrating through the LLM. OpenAI contrasts it with code.

options.text: Code is required, because an agent cannot hand work to another agent
options.explanation: OpenAI documents handoffs and agents used as tools. Code is one way to orchestrate, not a requirement.

options.text: Code makes the work more predictable in speed, cost and performance
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says orchestrating via code makes tasks more deterministic and predictable in speed, cost and performance.
